name: Times Literary Supplement cryptic crossword No 1,161

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Provoke offensive about Corbyn?

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: the Tet Offensive of 1968 in the Vietnam War
Jeremy Corbyn is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone tries to goad a political attack on the former Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Corbyn stands for any MP. TET is the Vietnamese New Year, best known from the Tet Offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to entice or goad them into acting, a verb synonym for stirring them up.

clue.text: The beginning of Forman’s Hollywood career

definitions.text: The beginning of Forman’s Hollywood career

blocks.clueFragment: The beginning of Forman’s Hollywood career
blocks.note: surface reading: the moment the director's American career got going
setter's reading: the title of Milos Forman's first American film, from 1971

explanation.walkthrough: Milos Forman, the Czech director of One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest, made his first American feature in 1971; its title also describes a career starting to soar.
explanation.definitionFit: A career that is taking off is beginning to succeed, and the phrase is also that film's actual title.

clue.text: …while entering Moscow’s her aim primarily

definitions.text: while entering Moscow’s her aim primarily

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so one piece is placed within the others
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters of the words are kept

blocks.note: opening letter of the city
as can mean while, as in 'as I was leaving'
opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A woman longs above all to reach Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the clue before it. In Chekhov's Three Sisters the sisters keep yearning to go to Moscow, so the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Masha is the middle sister in Chekhov's play Three Sisters, whose shared dream is returning to Moscow.

clue.text: After transactions I slept badly with such as 6, 21, 22D, and 27

indicators.note: done badly means done wrongly, so the letters end up in a muddled order
following something means coming next in line, so this piece is placed behind the other

blocks.note: TR is an abbreviation for transactions
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: After a day of business deals, someone had a poor night's sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references are all groups of three from Greek myth: the Furies, the Graces, the Fates and the Eumenides.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of those mythological groups has three members, so they are sets of three, or trios.

clue.text: Not in “Shaft” we hear, at least not at the same time

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken version, so the words are judged by their sound, not spelling

blocks.note: not in means out of, and a sink is a shaft dug downwards, as in mining

explanation.surface: Someone says they are not appearing in the film Shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaft looks like the 1971 detective film, but it is just a shaft dug into the ground, called a sink in mining.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are out of sync fail to coincide in timing, like a soundtrack lagging behind the picture.

clue.text: Gaol perhaps for the Beautiful Spy

indicators.note: perhaps signals one possible version of the letters, so they may be arranged differently

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged; gaol is the British spelling of jail

explanation.surface: A prison sentence might await a glamorous secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: Olga is also the eldest of Chekhov's Three Sisters, tying in with the puzzle's theme of trios.
explanation.definitionFit: Olga is a female first name, given here as that of a glamorous spy heroine.

clue.text: Torment Arnie suffered without some directions in this role?

definitions.text: Torment Arnie suffered without some directions in this role?

indicators.note: something that has suffered is knocked about, so its letters are jumbled
without means lacking, so certain letters are taken away

blocks.note: the letters to be worked on
east and north, two compass points

explanation.surface: Arnold Schwarzenegger had a tough time playing a particular part.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnie is Arnold Schwarzenegger, and the whole clue points to his most famous film part, the killer cyborg from 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: Schwarzenegger played the cyborg title character in James Cameron's film and its sequels.

clue.text: Their shrine‘s originally found at old city that’s at the foot of Acropolis

definitions.text: Their shrine‘s originally found at old city that’s at the foot of Acropolis

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only an opening letter is kept

blocks.note: opening letter of this word
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city
i.e. stands for id est, meaning that is
opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A guidebook note on where some goddesses were worshipped in ancient Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: The avenging goddesses had a cave shrine below the Areopagus, next to the Acropolis in Athens, so the whole clue describes them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Furies, or Erinyes, were the three Greek goddesses of vengeance worshipped at a shrine in Athens.

clue.text: “Trembles — ‘s ash yet standing” (Voluspa, Prophecy of the Seeress)

definitions.text: “Trembles — ‘s ash yet standing” (Voluspa, Prophecy of the Seeress)

blocks.note: surface reading: a line of verse with a gap left in it
setter's reading: the source tells you to fill the gap with the world tree of Norse myth

explanation.walkthrough: The Voluspa is an Old Norse poem in which a seeress foretells the end of the world; the dash marks the missing name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology the giant ash tree linking the nine worlds shakes at Ragnarok but stays upright.

clue.text: One of 3 amusing scapegoats, grumpy, making second a bit comical

indicators.note: making one thing into another means swapping it for something else
a bit of a word is just a small piece of it, here its opening letter

blocks.note: a synonym of bad-tempered
s is the abbreviation for second
opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: One of a trio of comic fall guys, a grouchy one who livens up for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 refers to the answer at 3 down. The Three Stooges were an American slapstick trio, always taking the blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Curly Howard was one of the Three Stooges, the comedy team who were forever on the receiving end.

clue.text: Did he go on trial, according to Hitchens, for just touching the Queen?

definitions.text: Did he go on trial, according to Hitchens

blocks.note: in snooker, balls just touching are said to be kissing
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A question whether someone was prosecuted for a minor brush with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Hitchens wrote The Trial of Henry Kissinger, a book arguing that Nixon's statesman should be tried for war crimes; he never actually went to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Kissinger is the subject of the polemic by Hitchens that puts him in the dock on paper only.

clue.text: Thursby, one of Cecil’s brothers-in-law

blocks.note: surface reading: a relative by marriage of someone called Cecil
setter's reading: Brothers in Law is a 1955 novel by Henry Cecil about young barristers

explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cecil was a judge who wrote comic legal novels; in Brothers in Law the hero is a newly qualified barrister surnamed Thursby.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Thursby is the young barrister at the centre of Henry Cecil's novel, later filmed by the Boulting brothers.

clue.text: “An End to Autumn” getting advance, more or less

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: final letter of this word
in advance means ahead of time, so early

explanation.surface: A book or poem titled An End to Autumn is published ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks dress the opening words up as a title; they are just an instruction to take a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and more or less are both adverbs meaning almost or approximately.

clue.text: How a score may appear: 51-11

blocks.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
the answer to 11 across

explanation.surface: A sports result printed as fifty-one to eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 51-11 looks like a match score but is a Roman numeral joined to a cross-reference. A score here is a scratched line.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a cut or scratched mark, which runs in a straight line, so it appears in linear fashion.

clue.text: Episode in which silent Tam gets in a tizzy about middle of dance

indicators.note: a tizzy is a state of agitation, so the letters are thrown into disorder
to be about something is to go round it, so the jumbled letters enclose another
the middle of a word is its central letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
central letter of this five-letter word

explanation.surface: A TV episode in which a quiet Scotsman gets flustered at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Tam is a Scottish form of Tom; here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An instalment is one part of a serial published or broadcast in sequence, which is an episode.

clue.text: , Like Cameron, one who fought the Battle of Waterloo?

definitions.note: adjectival phrase; the answer is a noun

definitions.text: one who fought the Battle of Waterloo?

blocks.note: first meaning: David Cameron, the former Prime Minister, was educated at Eton

blocks.clueFragment: one who fought the Battle of Waterloo?
blocks.note: second meaning: the saying that Waterloo was won on the playing fields of Eton

explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's best-known private boarding school; the Duke of Wellington is supposed to have said Waterloo was won on its playing fields.
explanation.definitionFit: A former pupil of Eton College is so called, a description fitting Cameron and, by the saying, Wellington's officers.

clue.text: Oracular bird, one going back and forth about back of grove

indicators.note: something going back and forth reads the same in both directions, a word that mirrors itself
the back of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept
to be about something is to surround it, so the pair encloses another letter

blocks.note: the extinct flightless bird of Mauritius
an means one; written backwards then forwards it reads the same both ways
final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A prophetic bird pacing to and fro around a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: One gives AN twice: once backwards, once forwards, with a letter between. Dodona's oracle spoke through the rustling of a sacred oak grove.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodona in Epirus held the oldest Greek oracle of Zeus, so the adjective describes anything prophetic in that style.

clue.text: A sparkling treat? It’s the tops!

definitions.text: A sparkling treat? It’s the tops!

indicators.note: the tops of words are their opening letters, which alone are kept

blocks.note: opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Praise for a fizzy indulgence as the very best.
explanation.walkthrough: It's the tops looks like slang for excellent, but it instructs you to take the opening letters of the words before it, which also describe the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy, a bubbly treat.

clue.text: Way stupid little girl returns to poets like Tennyson

indicators.note: returning means heading back to the start, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: St is short for street
a synonym
Di is a short form of Diana

explanation.surface: A foolish young girl goes back to reading Victorian poets.
explanation.walkthrough: Way stupid reads like slang for very stupid, but way and stupid are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson wrote Idylls of the King, so he is a writer of idylls, short pastoral or narrative poems.

clue.text: Patchett’s sonorous prose featured here?

blocks.note: surface reading: the book in which a novelist's resonant writing appears
setter's reading: the novel's title is also the Italian term for a style of rich, beautiful singing

explanation.walkthrough: Ann Patchett's 2001 novel, about an opera singer held hostage, takes its title from the Italian operatic singing style meaning beautiful song.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both Patchett's prize-winning novel and the smooth, lyrical vocal style of Italian opera.

clue.text: If returning to encounter tailless dog, it’ll be Abe Lincoln’s

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters run the other way
without a tail means losing its last letter
meeting something means coming up beside it, so the two pieces are joined

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: A puzzle about meeting a dog with no tail that belonged to the President.
explanation.walkthrough: Abe Lincoln's stands for his pet; the President's dog was famously named this, later the stock name for any dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln's yellow mongrel was called Fido, and he left it behind in Illinois when he went to Washington.

clue.text: Masters feature in Stoker broadcast drama

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a synonym

explanation.surface: Famous actors appear in a radio version of a Bram Stoker drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Masters looks like expert performers, but it is the golf tournament at Augusta.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masters golf tournament is scored by counting each player's total shots, the format called stroke play.

clue.text: Burns’s lassie’s leaving Italy with Greek trio

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: Gracie Allen was the wife and stage partner of the comedian George Burns
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl from a Robert Burns poem leaves Italy with three Greek companions.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns looks like the Scottish poet Robert Burns, but it is George Burns, the American comedian of Burns and Allen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Three Graces were the Greek goddesses of charm and beauty, a classic trio of sisters.

clue.text: Where real fun’s dispensed? Not likely!

definitions.text: Where real fun’s dispensed? Not likely!

indicators.note: dispensed means handed out in portions, so the letters are dealt out afresh

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sardonic question about places where enjoyment is handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the instruction and the joke: the last places anyone goes for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Burial services are solemn occasions of mourning, the opposite of entertainment, which the ironic definition plays on.

clue.text: Start to feel a setback under their influence?

definitions.text: Start to feel a setback under their influence?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept
back means going in the opposite direction, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: opening letter of this word
taken as written
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Someone begins to suffer a reverse while under some power's sway.
explanation.walkthrough: Setback reads as one word; it splits into a word and its direction. The whole clue hints at those who decide our misfortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fates were the three Greek goddesses who spun, measured and cut the thread of every human life.

clue.text: Where Sheridan was taught malicious gossip?

definitions.text: Where Sheridan was taught malicious gossip?

blocks.note: surface reading: the place where the playwright was educated
setter's reading: scandal, completing the title of Sheridan's 1777 comedy The ___ for Scandal

explanation.walkthrough: Richard Brinsley Sheridan wrote the comedy The School for Scandal, in which gossips trade malicious rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of teaching fits the first half, and the word completes the title of his best-known play.

clue.text: Salinger’s antihero ditching heroin one time

indicators.note: to ditch something is to get rid of it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: Holden Caulfield of The Catcher in the Rye
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: The troubled teenager of a famous novel gives up drugs for good.
explanation.walkthrough: One time is read as former or bygone, not as once only.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden and one-time both describe something belonging to the past, as in olden days, so they are adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Either of two novelists‘ European friends?

blocks.note: first meaning: Kingsley or his son Martin, both British novelists
second meaning: the French word for friends

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that European friends means friends in a European language, here French.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley and Martin, father and son, share this surname; in French the same word is the plural of ami, friend.

clue.text: One who’ll take tea, say, hot with crushed ice

indicators.note: say signals speech, so a word is replaced by a letter pronounced the same way
something crushed is broken up, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: the letter T is pronounced like this drink
H for hot, as on a tap
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who likes their tea iced, but served hot alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea serves twice, in the definition and as the sound of a letter. The answer is a rare word.
explanation.definitionFit: A theic is a person who drinks excessive amounts of tea, from thea, the old botanical name for the plant.

clue.text: 6 e.g. Greek chaps on a date

blocks.note: eu is the Greek for well or good, as in eulogy
a synonym
the Ides is a date in the Roman calendar, the 15th of March

explanation.surface: Some Greek men out together on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 refers to the answer at 6 down. The name means the kindly ones, a placating title for the avenging goddesses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eumenides is the euphemistic Greek name for the Furies, used as the title of Aeschylus's play.

clue.text: Pity, America is occupied by first sign of Trump’s ego – that may give them a headache

definitions.text: that may give them a headache

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept
a place occupied by people holds them inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: it's a sin means it's a pity
the United States
taken as written
opening letter of this word
ego is Latin for I

explanation.surface: A political complaint that America is in thrall to one man's vanity, enough to give anyone a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue before it: them is the cavities of the face, the sinuses inside the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinusitis is inflammation of the sinuses, a condition whose typical symptom is a pounding pain in the forehead.

clue.text: Were they not so badly hairy scary, according to Kipling?

definitions.text: Were they not so badly hairy scary, according to Kipling?

indicators.note: done badly means done wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether some creatures would be less frightening if they were less shaggy.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's barrack-room ballad Oonts calls the army camel the 'airy scary oont, mimicking the soldiers' dropped aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Oont is Anglo-Indian army slang for a camel, from Hindi, made famous by Kipling's poem.
